name: Lamborghini Murciélago LP580-4 E-Gear
description:
Named after a legendary fighting bull renowned for its courage and strength, the Lamborghini Murciélago ('Bat' in Spanish) arrived in 2001 as the worthy successor to the iconic Diablo. This was Lamborghini's first completely new design in eleven years and their inaugural model under Audi ownership—a partnership that brought German engineering precision to Italian supercar passion. Styled by Peruvian-born Belgian designer Luc Donckerwolke, the Murciélago's aggressive, angular bodywork featured the signature scissor doors and dramatic air intakes that announced its performance intentions from first glance.

At the heart of the Murciélago lies a magnificent 6.2-liter naturally aspirated V12 engine producing 572 horsepower at 7,500 rpm and 650 Nm of torque at 5,400 rpm. This longitudinally-mounted masterpiece features variable valve timing and a variable geometry intake manifold, allowing it to deliver brutal acceleration while maintaining the intoxicating V12 soundtrack that defines the Lamborghini experience. The E-Gear sequential manual transmission provides lightning-fast shifts via paddle shifters, offering modern convenience without sacrificing driver engagement.

Unlike its predecessor, the Murciélago employs a permanent all-wheel-drive system with a viscous center coupling that can vary torque distribution between 30/70 and 20/80 front-to-rear depending on conditions. This AWD system transforms the car's behavior, providing exceptional traction for launching and cornering while maintaining the rear-biased balance that makes it feel like a proper mid-engine supercar. The result is devastating performance: 0-100 km/h in just 3.8 seconds and a top speed of 331 km/h.

The chassis combines a steel spaceframe with carbon fiber and composite body panels, achieving remarkable rigidity while keeping weight to 1,650 kg. Independent double wishbone suspension at all four corners, massive ventilated disc brakes (365mm front, 355mm rear), and wide Pirelli P Zero tires (245/35ZR18 front, 335/30ZR18 rear) provide the dynamic capabilities expected of a flagship Lamborghini. The adjustable rear spoiler automatically deploys at speed, balancing aerodynamics between maximum downforce and minimum drag.

From 2001 to 2010, Lamborghini produced 4,099 Murciélagos across various iterations, with this model representing the pure essence of early-2000s supercar design—naturally aspirated V12 power, all-wheel-drive grip, and dramatic Italian styling that still turns heads today. The Murciélago proved that Lamborghini could compete with the best supercars in the world while maintaining its unique character and soul.
